# NBA 75th Anniversary Team

As selected in 2021 by a blue-ribbon panel of current and former NBA players, coaches, general managers and team and league executives, WNBA legends and sportswriters and broadcasters.

Voters were asked to select the 75 Greatest Players in NBA History without regard to position. Panelists did not rank their selections.

Current and former players were not allowed to vote for themselves.

# NBA 75th Anniversary Team NBA 75th Anniversary Team Top 76 NBA players in the history of the NBA "NBA 75" redirects here. For the NBA's 75th anniversary season, see [2021–22 NBA season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_NBA_season "2021–22 NBA season"). [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bc/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team_%28cropped%29.jpg/960px-NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team_%28cropped%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team_(cropped).jpg) Members of the NBA 75th Anniversary Team during the halftime ceremony of the [2022 NBA All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NBA_All-Star_Game "2022 NBA All-Star Game"). The **NBA 75th Anniversary Team**, also referred to as the **NBA 75**,[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team#cite_note-2) was chosen in 2021 to honor [the 75th anniversary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_NBA_season#75th_anniversary_promotions "2021–22 NBA season") of the founding of the [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA). It was the fourth and most recent [anniversary team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_anniversary_teams "NBA anniversary teams") in the league.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team#cite_note-3) Similar to the [50 Greatest Players in NBA History](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/50_Greatest_Players_in_NBA_History "50 Greatest Players in NBA History") named in 1996, a panel of reporters, current and former players, coaches, general managers, and team executives selected the greatest players in league history.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team#cite_note-nbafaq-4) Tasked with compiling a list of 75 players, the committee named an additional 76th member due to a tie in voting.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team#cite_note-golliver_10202021-5)[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team#cite_note-6) It was billed as part of the league's anniversary celebration during the [2021–22 NBA season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_NBA_season "2021–22 NBA season").[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team#cite_note-nbafaq-4) Forty-five of the seventy-six players were later assembled in [Cleveland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland "Cleveland"), during the halftime ceremony of the [2022 All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NBA_All-Star_Game "2022 NBA All-Star Game").[\[note 1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team#cite_note-7) ## Players selected ### List At the time of selection, the players selected combined for 158 [NBA championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Finals "NBA Finals"), 62 [Most Valuable Player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "NBA Most Valuable Player Award") (MVP) awards, 48 [Finals MVP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Finals_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "NBA Finals Most Valuable Player Award") awards, and 730 [All-Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_All-Star_Game "NBA All-Star Game") selections. Of the 76 players, all 50 members of the 50th anniversary team were selected.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team#cite_note-nba_1022021-8) The other 26 included players from the 1970s to the current era.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team#cite_note-9) Two notable omissions from the earlier top 50 selections, [Bob McAdoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_McAdoo "Bob McAdoo") and [Dominique Wilkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominique_Wilkins "Dominique Wilkins"), were named to the 75th anniversary list.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team#cite_note-10)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team#cite_note-kalbrosky_10212021-11) When the previous 50 players were chosen in 1996–97, Wilkins was the only nine-time All-Star to be excluded, as well as the only six-time [All-NBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-NBA "All-NBA") selection to miss the cut. [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/Phil_Jackson_3_cropped.jpg/330px-Phil_Jackson_3_cropped.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Phil_Jackson_3_cropped.jpg) [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b5/Auerbach_Lipofsky.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Auerbach_Lipofsky.jpg) [Phil Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Jackson "Phil Jackson") (left) and [Red Auerbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Auerbach "Red Auerbach") (right) both made the 2022 list of the 15 greatest coaches in NBA history. Alongside the selection of the NBA's 75th anniversary team was the selection of the 15 Greatest Coaches in NBA History. The list was compiled based upon unranked selection undertaken exclusively by a panel of 43 current and former NBA coaches in collaboration with the National Basketball Coaches Association. Of the 15 coaches, eight members of the [Top 10 Coaches in NBA History](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/50_Greatest_Players_in_NBA_History#Top_10_Coaches_in_NBA_History "50 Greatest Players in NBA History") in 1996 were selected; original Top 10 coaches [Bill Fitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Fitch "Bill Fitch") and [John Kundla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kundla "John Kundla") were excluded from the updated list. Nine of the 15 coaches named were alive at the time of the list's announcement, and four of them— [Steve Kerr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Kerr "Steve Kerr"), [Gregg Popovich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregg_Popovich "Gregg Popovich"), [Doc Rivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doc_Rivers "Doc Rivers"), and [Erik Spoelstra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erik_Spoelstra "Erik Spoelstra")—were active.[\[note 9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team#cite_note-108) Since then, Popovich and Rivers retired in 2025 and 2026 respectively and [Lenny Wilkens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenny_Wilkens "Lenny Wilkens") died in 2025.[\[100\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team#cite_note-109) The other deceased coaches are [Red Holzman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Holzman "Red Holzman") in 1998,[\[101\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team#cite_note-110) [Red Auerbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Auerbach "Red Auerbach") in 2006,[\[102\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team#cite_note-111) [Chuck Daly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Daly "Chuck Daly") in 2009,[\[103\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team#cite_note-112) [Jack Ramsay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Ramsay "Jack Ramsay") in 2014,[\[104\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team#cite_note-113) and both [K. C. Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._C._Jones "K. C. Jones") and [Jerry Sloan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Sloan "Jerry Sloan") in 2020.[\[105\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team#cite_note-114)[\[106\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team#cite_note-115) Sloan and [Don Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Nelson "Don Nelson") were the only members to never win a championship as a coach; Nelson won five as a player. Wilkens is the only person named to both the coaches and players lists, doing so for both the 50th and 75th anniversary lists. At the time of selection, 10 of the 15 coaches were members of the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame as a coach. Nelson was the most recent inductee at the time, inducted in 2012. metadata.ogDescription: The NBA 75th Anniversary Team, also referred to as the NBA 75, was chosen in 2021 to honor the 75th anniversary of the founding of the National Basketball Association (NBA). It was the fourth and most recent anniversary team in the league. Similar to the 50 Greatest Players in NBA History named in 1996, a panel of reporters, current and former players, coaches, general managers, and team executives selected the greatest players in league history. Tasked with compiling a list of 75 players, the committee named an additional 76th member due to a tie in voting. It was billed as part of the league's anniversary celebration during the 2021–22 NBA season. Forty-five of the seventy-six players were later assembled in Cleveland, during the halftime ceremony of the 2022 All-Star Game.
